In other words, the High Court
must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to
continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal proceeding
would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise
between the victim and wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is
appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above
question(s) is in affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to
quash the criminal proceeding."

the exercise of the power under Section 482 and while dealing with a plea that the dispute has been

FIR no.214 dated 05.10.2017 as well as its connected DDR no.30 dated 10.2017. Kaushalya Sawhney, , at P 642, Hon'ble Supreme Court
observed that the finest hour of Justice arises propitiously when parties, who fell apart, bury the
hatchet and weave a sense of fellowship or reunion. The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus:
the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint
in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given toAmritpal Singh And Ors vs State Of Punjab And Anr on 10 January, 2023
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166578427/ 5
a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code. Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be
exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz; (i) to secure the
ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court. 6 of 12 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:003179 CRM-M-14119-2018 (O&M) &
CRM-M-14066-2018 (O&M) -7- However, before exercise of such power, the High
Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime. In this category of cases, High Court may quash
criminal proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise between the offender
and victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of
criminal case would put accused to great oppression and prejudice and extreme
injustice would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal case despite full and
complete settlement and compromise with the victim. It only recognises and preserves powers which inhere in the High
Court;
16.2 The invocation of the jurisdiction of the High Court to quash a First Information
Report or a criminal proceeding on the ground that a settlement has been arrived at
between the offender and the victim is not the same as the invocation of jurisdiction
for the purpose of compounding an offence.

The object of law is well served when the parties resolve their differences and chose to peacefully
